concrete_capability_transition: CLI list tasks and mode list change from sparse skeleton command output to bounded, runtime-owned progress and mode UX that surfaces next actions without the CLI taking policy authority.

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Makes brownie list tasks usable for a headless caller or human operator to see runnable, blocked, terminal, parent-join, and next-action state before choosing run/resume/inspect.
Makes brownie mode list executable through the runtime-owned mode.list method so the CLI displays compiled mode policy without discovering or interpreting Mode Packs itself.
Projects the existing runtime progress_overview into bounded human text while preserving the runtime result for later stable JSON work.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, runtime_permission_enforcement, and progress_visualization by exposing runtime-owned progress and mode summaries through usable CLI commands.
answers.new_capability: A user can run brownie list tasks to see runnable, blocked, terminal, parent-join, grouped next-action, and route-candidate state, and brownie mode list now calls runtime mode.list instead of returning unsupported.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: CLI-1 through CLI-5 made commands parse and run/resume executable, but list tasks only printed sparse counts and mode list was still an unsupported skeleton despite the runtime already owning mode.list.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Headless operators would still lack a bounded next-action view from the CLI and could not inspect available runtime modes without falling back to non-CLI tooling.
answers.non_duplicative: This is not another run/resume or report phase: it changes user-visible CLI behavior for task progress and mode listing while delegating all policy and progress computation to existing runtime RPCs.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase uses existing task.list and mode.list and adds no JSON-RPC method, passthrough, or mirror surface.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It consumes existing progress_overview and ModeSummary structures; it does not add readiness, digest, history, verdict, or summary documents as product behavior.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: User-visible CLI behavior changes: mode list becomes executable through runtime mode.list, and list tasks renders the runtime progress_overview groups and candidates with bounded deterministic truncation.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: The CLI can now show a caller what can be resumed, inspected, or acted on next without duplicating runtime selection policy, improving safe autonomous control-plane operation.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the CLI-6 progress and next-action UX gap while leaving stable public JSON, packaging, arbitrary-repository golden journey, and restart/recovery golden journey to later phases.

accepted_capability: CLI task progress output surfaces runtime-owned next-action and route state in bounded human text.
CLI mode list is executable through Rust runtime mode.list while keeping Mode Pack and permission authority in the runtime.
behavior_evidence: Fake runtime tests cover rich progress, bounds, JSON compatibility, and sensitive route reason suppression.
Fake and real runtime tests cover mode.list invocation and output.
Existing command tests preserve run/resume/status/inspect behavior.
safety_boundary: No Core Runtime terminal campaign state is reopened or mutated.
No new runtime JSON-RPC method is added.
The CLI does not read ledgers, discover Mode Packs from files, evaluate permissions, select tasks, apply patches, or own recovery policy.
Human output remains bounded and excludes raw prompts, provider responses, file content, stdout/stderr payloads, commands, environment values, paths, and secrets.
non_goals: No stable full public JSON projection overhaul or exit-code redesign.
No arbitrary-repository golden journey or restart/recovery golden journey closure.
No Mode Pack, Product DoD, provider, permission, workspace mutation, replay, or fail-closed semantic redesign.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected CLI-side task eligibility selection because next execution policy belongs to the Rust runtime.
Rejected CLI-owned Mode Pack file discovery because mode policy is runtime authority.
Rejected adding a new progress RPC because task.list already returns runtime-owned progress_overview.
Rejected rewriting --json output in this phase because CLI-7 owns stable bounded public JSON semantics.
technical_debt: CLI-7 must define stable public JSON projections and exit code semantics.
CLI-9 must validate the arbitrary-repository golden journey.
CLI-10 must validate restart/recovery including scoped resume.
next_capability_rationale: After CLI-6 lands, proceed to CLI-7 Human / JSON Output and Exit Codes rather than adding another progress wrapper.
